text.p: AO Surgutneftegaz will seek permission from shareholders on March 22 to raise its authorised capital to 6.16 trillion roubles from 6.00 trillion currently, a senior company official said on Monday.

Capital would be increased by issuing 166 million preferred shares, Andrei Serebryakov, head of the securities department at the company's biggest shareholder, NK Surgutneftegaz (Surgut Holding), told Reuters.

The object of the increase is to restore the proportion of ordinary to preferred stock to 75:25, which is usual for Russian companies, Serebryakov said. Preferred shares currently make up about 22.1 percent of Surgutneftegaz's capital, he said.
It was not yet decided when or whether the company would actually issue the shares, once it had received permission from shareholders to increase authorised capital.
At 1110 GMT Surgut ordinaries were last traded on the Russian Trading System at $0.765 and the prefs were $0.550 after closing on Friday at $0.745 and $0.525 respectively.
